sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》负责商业和政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上，现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼等众多嘉宾。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 届时，您可以观看其中一些毫无保留、未经修饰的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, Robert Mueller breaks his silence.
sentences.zh: 今天，罗伯特·穆勒打破了沉默。

sentences.en: Quote, if we had had confidence that the president clearly did not commit a crime, we would have said so.
sentences.zh: 引用他的话：“如果我们确信总统显然没有犯罪，我们早就这么说了。”

sentences.en: It's Thursday, May 30th.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月30日，星期四。

sentences.en: Guys, I'm here.
sentences.zh: 伙计们，我到了。

sentences.en: Mike.
sentences.zh: 迈克。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 在。

sentences.en: Hey.
sentences.zh: 嘿。

sentences.en: Schmidt.
sentences.zh: 施密特。

sentences.en: Hold on, I got to take the headphones off for a second.
sentences.zh: 等一下，我得先把耳机摘下来。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Mike Schmidt, so what happens on Wednesday morning?
sentences.zh: 迈克·施密特，周三早上发生了什么？

sentences.en: Around 9.30 a.m., the special counsel's office sends out an email saying that Robert Mueller will be holding a press conference in an hour and a half.
sentences.zh: 大约上午9点30分，特别检察官办公室发出一封邮件，称罗伯特·穆勒将在一个半小时后举行新闻发布会。

sentences.en: This will be a statement only, no question and answer period to follow.
sentences.zh: 这仅是一份声明，之后不会有问答环节。

sentences.en: We had not heard Robert Mueller's voice in the two years that he led this investigation.
sentences.zh: 在穆勒领导这项调查的两年里，我们从未听过他的声音。

sentences.en: No press conferences, no public statements on courthouse steps, no media interviews, nothing.
sentences.zh: 没有新闻发布会，没有在法院台阶上发表公开声明，没有媒体采访，什么都没有。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, he's going to talk.
sentences.zh: 而突然之间，他要开口说话了。

sentences.en: I feel like I don't even know his voice, and we're a show where you kind of instinctively know everyone's voice after a while, and I couldn't even tell you what Robert Mueller's
sentences.zh: 我觉得我甚至不知道他的声音是什么样的，而我们这个节目，听久了大家的声音都会有一种本能的熟悉感，但我甚至说不出罗伯特·穆勒的

sentences.en: voice sounds like.
sentences.zh: 声音听起来是什么样。

sentences.en: Well, in Washington, his voice is fairly familiar because he was the FBI director for 12 years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在华盛顿，他的声音其实很熟悉，因为他担任了12年的联邦调查局局长。

sentences.en: He was a very public figure.
sentences.zh: 他曾是一位非常公开的人物。

sentences.en: But during this investigation, he said nothing.
sentences.zh: 但在这次调查期间，他什么也没说。

sentences.en: He let the indictments speak for themselves.
sentences.zh: 他让起诉书自己说话。

sentences.en: Occasionally, when a really high-profile moment came, the deputy attorney general, Rod Rosenstein, would say something publicly.
sentences.zh: 偶尔，当出现非常引人注目的时刻时，副司法部长罗德·罗森斯坦会公开说些什么。

sentences.en: But all we really knew about Mueller over the past two years were these snippets that sort of eked out.
sentences.zh: 但过去两年里，我们对穆勒真正了解的，只有那些零星流出的片段。

sentences.en: Early this morning, special counsel Robert Mueller was spotted arriving in his office building in Washington, as we expect him to finish his report any day now.
sentences.zh: 今天清晨，特别检察官罗伯特·穆勒被拍到抵达华盛顿的办公大楼，我们预计他很快就会完成报告。

sentences.en: Someone would see Mueller walking down the street.
sentences.zh: 有人会看到穆勒走在街上。

sentences.en: Oh, I saw Mueller today.
sentences.zh: 哦，我今天看到穆勒了。

sentences.en: Some breaking news for you this morning.
sentences.zh: 今早为您带来一些突发新闻。

sentences.en: Special counsel Robert Mueller was just spotted this morning coming out of church.
sentences.zh: 特别检察官罗伯特·穆勒今早刚被拍到从教堂出来。

sentences.en: Mueller was seen going to church.
sentences.zh: 有人看到穆勒去教堂了。

sentences.en: He was seen going to his favorite restaurant.
sentences.zh: 有人看到他去了他最喜欢的餐厅。

sentences.en: Guys, get this.
sentences.zh: 伙计们，听着。

sentences.en: Yesterday, Robert Mueller was spotted at an Apple store when he said his computer is really slow.
sentences.zh: 昨天，罗伯特·穆勒被发现在一家苹果商店，当时他说他的电脑运行非常慢。

sentences.en: The employee said, like, normal slow or your investigation slow?
sentences.zh: 员工问，是正常的慢，还是你们调查的那种慢？

sentences.en: But we heard nothing from him.
sentences.zh: 但我们没从他那里听到任何消息。

sentences.en: Mueller wouldn't say anything.
sentences.zh: 穆勒什么也不肯说。

sentences.en: There was an upside to this silence.
sentences.zh: 这种沉默也有积极的一面。

sentences.en: By saying nothing, Mueller appeared above the fray.
sentences.zh: 通过保持沉默，穆勒显得超然于纷争之外。

sentences.en: He did not appear to be overly political.
sentences.zh: 他看起来并不显得过于政治化。

sentences.en: He did not appear to be trying to manipulate the media.
sentences.zh: 他看起来并不像是在试图操纵媒体。

sentences.en: He sort of was beyond reproach because of that.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，他似乎无可指责。

sentences.en: But there was a downside to it.
sentences.zh: 但这也存在负面影响。

sentences.en: The president tweeting this morning, quote, disgraced and discredited Bob Mueller and his whole group of angry Democrat thugs spent over 30 hours with the White House counsel.
sentences.zh: 总统今早发推文称，引用：“名誉扫地、信誉破产的鲍勃·穆勒和他那群愤怒的民主党暴徒，与白宫法律顾问谈了30多个小时。”

sentences.en: During all these periods of silence, the president exploited that void.
sentences.zh: 在所有这些沉默的时期，总统利用了这一真空。

sentences.en: The special counsel completed its report and found no collusion and no obstruction, total exoneration.
sentences.zh: 特别检察官完成了报告，发现没有勾结，也没有妨碍司法，完全洗清了嫌疑。

sentences.en: And then once the report is actually completed, of course, Attorney General Bill Barr steps into the void as well with his take on what Mueller found.
sentences.zh: 而当报告真正完成后，司法部长比尔·巴尔当然也介入了这个真空，并对穆勒的发现提出了自己的看法。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: After carefully reviewing the facts and legal theories outlined in the report, the deputy attorney general and I concluded that the evidence developed by the special counsel is
sentences.zh: 在仔细审查了报告中概述的事实和法律理论后，副司法部长和我得出结论，特别检察官收集的证据

sentences.en: not sufficient to establish that the president committed an obstruction of justice offense.
sentences.zh: 不足以证明总统犯有妨碍司法罪。

sentences.en: So when we hear this morning that Mueller is going to speak for the first time, it's like, what the heck is he going to say?
sentences.zh: 所以当我们今早听说穆勒要首次公开发言时，大家都在想，他到底要说什么？

sentences.en: Is he going to try and clarify the way that the president and Barr characterized his investigation?
sentences.zh: 他会试图澄清总统和巴尔对他的调查所做的定性吗？

sentences.en: What is it that is such a big deal that Bob Mueller is going to break his silence?
sentences.zh: 鲍勃·穆勒打破沉默，究竟有什么大不了的事？

sentences.en: Well, good morning, everyone, and thank you for being here.
sentences.zh: 嗯，大家早上好，感谢大家的到来。

sentences.en: So Mueller, on time, walks out at 11 a.m.
sentences.zh: 所以，穆勒准时在上午11点走了出来。

sentences.en: He basically says the investigation's over.
sentences.zh: 他基本上宣布调查结束了。

sentences.en: We're closing up shop.
sentences.zh: 我们要收摊了。

sentences.en: We are formally closing the special counsel's office.
sentences.zh: 我们正式关闭特别检察官办公室。

sentences.en: And as well, I'm resigning from the Department of Justice to return to private life.
sentences.zh: 同时，我将辞去司法部的职务，回归私人生活。

sentences.en: I'm retiring, and if you have questions about the report, read it, because there's not much that I can add to what's in there.
sentences.zh: 我要退休了，如果你们对报告有疑问，请去读报告，因为我能补充的内容不多。

sentences.en: But beyond these few remarks, it is important that the office's written work speak for itself.
sentences.zh: 除了这几句简短的发言外，重要的是让办公室的书面工作本身来说话。

sentences.en: And then he dives deep into the obstruction part of the report.
sentences.zh: 然后他深入探讨了报告中关于妨碍司法的部分。

sentences.en: The question about whether the president tried to impede the investigation.
sentences.zh: 关于总统是否试图阻挠调查的问题。

sentences.en: And there, he really gets into an explanation of why his office did not make a determination about whether the president broke the law.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他真正解释了为什么他的办公室没有就总统是否触犯法律做出定论。

sentences.en: And this is arguably the greatest source of confusion to people.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是人们感到困惑的最大根源。

sentences.en: So what does Mueller say?
sentences.zh: 那么穆勒是怎么说的？

sentences.en: The special counsel's office is part of the Department of Justice, and by regulation, it was bound by that department policy.
sentences.zh: 特别检察官办公室是司法部的一部分，根据规定，它受该部门政策的约束。

sentences.en: Charging the president with a crime was therefore not an option we could consider.
sentences.zh: 因此，起诉总统犯罪不是我们可以考虑的选项。

sentences.en: The simple version of it is that because there's a Justice Department policy that says you cannot
sentences.zh: 简单来说，因为司法部有一项政策规定，你不能

sentences.en: indict a sitting president, it would be wrong and unfair to even accuse a sitting president of breaking
sentences.zh: 起诉在任总统，所以即使指控在任总统触犯法律也是错误且不公平的，

sentences.en: the law because the president would have no ability to go to court to clear their name.
sentences.zh: 因为总统将无法通过法庭来洗清自己的名声。

sentences.en: Then, Mueller says something that is in the report.
sentences.zh: 然后，穆勒说了一些报告里已经有的内容。

sentences.en: But when we hear it from him, it is even more powerful.
sentences.zh: 但当我们亲耳听到他说出来时，感觉更加震撼。

sentences.en: If we had had confidence that the president clearly did not commit a crime, we would have said so.
sentences.zh: 如果我们确信总统显然没有犯罪，我们早就这么说了。

sentences.en: We did not, however, make a determination as to whether the president did commit a crime.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们并没有就总统是否犯罪做出定论。

sentences.en: He essentially says, if we didn't think the president broke the law, we would say that.
sentences.zh: 他本质上是在说，如果我们认为总统没有触犯法律，我们就会说出来。

sentences.en: And we're not saying that.
sentences.zh: 而我们并没有那样说。

sentences.en: Because Mueller is so literal, we have to read between the lines.
sentences.zh: 因为穆勒说话非常字面化，我们必须解读他的言外之意。

sentences.en: We can't accuse the president of breaking the law because he's the president.
sentences.zh: 我们不能指控总统触犯法律，因为他是总统。

sentences.en: If we could clear him, we would.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能证明他清白，我们早就做了。

sentences.en: And there's sort of only one logical conclusion.
sentences.zh: 所以只有一个逻辑结论。

sentences.en: Which is that the president obstructed justice.
sentences.zh: 那就是总统妨碍了司法。

sentences.en: That Mueller thinks the president obstructed justice.
sentences.zh: 穆勒认为总统妨碍了司法。

sentences.en: My sense is that when Bill Barr first came out and began to describe what was going to be in this
sentences.zh: 我的感觉是，当比尔·巴尔第一次出来开始描述这份报告的内容，

sentences.en: report and then characterize it once the report was out, his strong implication was that
sentences.zh: 并在报告发布后对其进行定性时，他强烈暗示，

sentences.en: the reason why Mueller didn't make that determination is because there wasn't evidence of it.
sentences.zh: 穆勒没有做出那个定论的原因是因为没有证据。

sentences.en: And there wasn't evidence of an underlying crime to obstruct, not because of this Department of Justice rule.
sentences.zh: 而且没有妨碍司法的潜在犯罪证据，而不是因为这条司法部规则。

sentences.en: Barr specifically said when he released the report that Mueller had told him that the Justice
sentences.zh: 巴尔在发布报告时明确表示，穆勒曾告诉他，司法部

sentences.en: Department policy about indicting a president had not played a factor in their decision.
sentences.zh: 关于起诉总统的政策并没有在他们的决定中起到作用。

sentences.en: Special counsel Mueller stated three times to us in that meeting in response to our questioning
sentences.zh: 特别检察官穆勒在会议中回应我们的提问时曾三次向我们明确表示，

sentences.en: that he emphatically was not saying that but for the OLC opinion, he would have found obstruction.
sentences.zh: 他绝不是在说，如果不是因为法律顾问办公室的意见，他就会认定存在妨碍司法。

sentences.en: But what Mueller is saying pretty clearly right here on Wednesday morning in front of these live
sentences.zh: 但穆勒在周三早上当着这些电视摄像机的面，非常清楚地表达的是：我相信总统触犯了法律，

sentences.en: television cameras is, I believe the president committed a crime regardless of why he chose to charge him or not charge him.
sentences.zh: 无论他选择起诉还是不起诉的原因是什么。

sentences.en: He all but says that, yes.
sentences.zh: 他几乎就是这么说的，是的。

sentences.en: If you listen to what he says and follow his points to their rational conclusion, that's where you end up.
sentences.zh: 如果你听他说了什么，并顺着他的观点推导到合理的结论，这就是你最终得出的结果。

sentences.en: I feel like clear communication has not been emphasized enough throughout this process.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在整个过程中，清晰的沟通并没有得到足够的重视。

sentences.en: It's clear from what Mueller has done over the past two years that he thought that if he laid things out in writing, the facts would stand for themselves.
sentences.zh: 从穆勒过去两年的做法可以清楚看出，他认为只要把事情写下来，事实就会不言自明。

sentences.en: And here we are two years in, and I'm not sure that has been proven true.
sentences.zh: 而现在两年过去了，我不确定这是否被证明是正确的。

sentences.en: We may not live in that era anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们可能不再生活在那个时代了。

sentences.en: We may live in a time where you may actually need a bit of a James Comey approach.
sentences.zh: 我们可能生活在一个你确实需要一点詹姆斯·科米式方法的时代。

sentences.en: Really drive the narrative behind what you believe the facts are because the facts have not always held on their own.
sentences.zh: 真正去推动你所认定的事实背后的叙事，因为事实并不总是能站得住脚。

sentences.en: And the political winds here are so strong that they may knock down some of the facts and make it harder for what Mueller wanted the message to be to come through.
sentences.zh: 这里的政治风向太强了，它们可能会推翻一些事实，使穆勒想要传达的信息更难被理解。

sentences.en: Now, that may have turned out to be a miscalculation.
sentences.zh: 现在看来，这可能是一个误判。

sentences.en: Members of his team are disappointed by how the report has been received.
sentences.zh: 他的团队成员对报告所受到的反响感到失望。

sentences.en: And if Mueller had been someone like Jim Comey, who was never going to allow anyone else to sculpt the narrative of his work, would we be in a different place?
sentences.zh: 如果穆勒是像吉姆·科米那样的人，从不让别人来塑造他工作的叙事，我们会处于不同的境地吗？

sentences.en: Had Mueller been more aggressive, more forward-leaning, more explicit in his report,
sentences.zh: 如果穆勒更激进、更积极、在报告中更明确，

sentences.en: would that have made it more difficult for Barr to have done the things that he did?
sentences.zh: 那会让他人更难像巴尔那样行事吗？

sentences.en: And would it have had more of an impact on the public discourse around whether the president broke the law and should be impeached?
sentences.zh: 这会对公众关于总统是否触犯法律以及是否应该被弹劾的讨论产生更大的影响吗？

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果您还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用程序，并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So after laying out a case for why he thinks the president has committed obstruction of justice, where does Mueller go from there?
sentences.zh: 那么在阐述了他认为总统妨碍司法的理由之后，穆勒接下来要做什么？

sentences.en: There is a logical question, if you're following at home, that if the president can't be charged, why do the investigation?
sentences.zh: 如果你在家里关注这件事，会有一个逻辑问题：如果总统不能被起诉，为什么要进行调查？

sentences.en: So he explains that.
sentences.zh: 所以他解释了这一点。

sentences.en: He says that even though the Justice Department policies say you can't charge the president, you can investigate him and you can investigate him because.
sentences.zh: 他说，尽管司法部政策规定不能起诉总统，但你可以调查他，之所以可以调查他，是因为。

sentences.en: First, the opinion explicitly permits the investigation of a sitting president because it is important to preserve evidence while memories are fresh and documents available.
sentences.zh: 首先，该意见明确允许对在任总统进行调查，因为在记忆尚新、文件可得的情况下保存证据非常重要。

sentences.en: You need to preserve the evidence in real time to make sure people's memories are still fresh to get a real take on what may have gone wrong.
sentences.zh: 你需要实时保存证据，以确保人们的记忆依然清晰，从而对可能出错的事情有一个真实的了解。

sentences.en: And it makes you wonder.
sentences.zh: 这让人不禁好奇。

sentences.en: It's like, OK, well, why do you need to collect the evidence now?
sentences.zh: 就像是，好吧，为什么现在需要收集证据？

sentences.en: If you can't charge the president now, what does that mean you think could happen when the president leaves office?
sentences.zh: 如果你现在不能起诉总统，那意味着你认为总统离任后会发生什么？

sentences.en: So what Mueller is saying is, why do we do an investigation of the president even if we can't charge the president?
sentences.zh: 所以穆勒的意思是，即使我们不能起诉总统，为什么还要调查他？

sentences.en: Because someday he might not be president.
sentences.zh: 因为总有一天他可能不再是总统了。

sentences.en: An obstruction of justice investigation into the president's firing of Jim Comey in 2017 is much easier in 2017 and 2018 and 2019 than it would be in 2021 if the president were
sentences.zh: 对总统在2017年解雇吉姆·科米一事进行妨碍司法调查，在2017年、2018年和2019年要比在2021年总统离任后容易得多。

sentences.en: to leave office.
sentences.zh: 如果他离任的话。

sentences.en: Mike, how does this news conference come to an end?
sentences.zh: 迈克，这场新闻发布会是怎么结束的？

sentences.en: Now, I hope and expect this to be the only time that I will speak to you in this manner.
sentences.zh: 现在，我希望并期待这是我唯一一次以这种方式与你们交谈。

sentences.en: I am making that decision myself.
sentences.zh: 这个决定是我自己做出的。

sentences.en: No one has told me whether I can or should testify or speak further about this matter.
sentences.zh: 没有人告诉我我是否可以或应该就此事作证或进一步发言。

sentences.en: He basically acknowledges that there is a desire for him to testify publicly on Capitol Hill and then says any testimony from this office would not go beyond our report.
sentences.zh: 他基本上承认了人们希望他在国会山公开作证，然后说来自本办公室的任何证词都不会超出我们的报告范围。

sentences.en: Everything that I would say is in the report.
sentences.zh: 我所能说的一切都在报告里了。

sentences.en: What's the real need for calling me up there to speak?
sentences.zh: 叫我去那里发言还有什么真正的必要吗？

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you for being here today.
sentences.zh: 感谢大家今天的到来。

sentences.en: Why do you think that Mueller is so definitive here in saying that he will not testify?
sentences.zh: 你认为穆勒在这里如此肯定地说他不会作证，原因是什么？

sentences.en: Because Congress, especially the Democratic chairman of these oversight committees, say that they want him to testify.
sentences.zh: 因为国会，尤其是这些监督委员会的民主党主席们，都说他们希望他出面作证。

sentences.en: And you would think that he would welcome a chance to clarify any confusion and explain this investigation he spent two years overseeing.
sentences.zh: 你本以为他会乐于借此机会澄清任何困惑，并解释他花了两年时间监督的这项调查。

sentences.en: I think it's still one of the great mysteries of what's going on right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为这仍然是目前正在发生的事情中的一大谜团。

sentences.en: Robert Mueller has probably testified before Congress more so than any other American.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·穆勒在国会作证的次数可能比任何其他美国人都多。

sentences.en: FBI director for 12 years was likely testifying at least twice a quarter.
sentences.zh: 作为联邦调查局局长，他在12年里很可能每个季度至少作证两次。

sentences.en: So that's two, four, six, eight, eight times a year for 12 years.
sentences.zh: 所以那是两年，四次，六次，八次，一年八次，持续了12年。

sentences.en: He's got a team of folks that worked on something for two years and think at the very least that
sentences.zh: 他有一支团队，他们为此工作了两年，并且至少认为

sentences.en: Barr has mischaracterized or downplayed their findings.
sentences.zh: 巴尔歪曲或淡化了他们的调查结果。

sentences.en: But he's not going to testify?
sentences.zh: 但他不打算作证？

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Instead, we get an eight minute or so press statement in which he doesn't take questions and essentially rereads different sections of the report.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们只得到了一份大约八分钟的媒体声明，他在声明中不接受提问，本质上只是重读了报告的不同章节。

sentences.en: So why do you think he won't testify?
sentences.zh: 那么你认为他为什么不作证呢？

sentences.en: You've just laid out all the reasons why it would be logical for him to show up before one of these congressional committees.
sentences.zh: 你刚才列举了所有他出现在这些国会委员会面前的逻辑理由。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: And he's not going to ever explain it.
sentences.zh: 而且他永远不会解释原因。

sentences.en: Well, if you heard him today, I don't think we're ever going to hear from him again.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你今天听了他的话，我不认为我们以后还能再听到他的声音。

sentences.en: It's not like he's going to go on a speaking tour and write a book and go on Colbert and go on the Daily.
sentences.zh: 他可不是那种会去巡回演讲、写书、上科尔伯特节目或上《每日秀》的人。

sentences.en: That's not going to happen.
sentences.zh: 那是不可能发生的。

sentences.en: We saw today, though, the power of him simply saying out loud what's in the report.
sentences.zh: 不过，我们今天看到了他仅仅大声说出报告内容所产生的力量。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, he didn't say anything today that he didn't say in the report.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他今天说的任何话，他在报告里都已经说过了。

sentences.en: He just said it in public.
sentences.zh: 他只是在公开场合说了出来。

sentences.en: On television where the average person could digest it.
sentences.zh: 在电视上，普通人都能听懂的地方。

sentences.en: So if you're the Democrats and you saw that today,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是民主党人，并且今天看到了那一幕，

sentences.en: you think, man, we'd really like to get him up here because if he was able to sort of shake the trees and move the debate and
sentences.zh: 你会想，天哪，我们真的很想让他到这里来，因为如果他能够以某种方式敲山震虎并推动辩论，而且

sentences.en: we've seen the discussion on this move in just the hour since it happened, what would the impact be of him testifying for many hours publicly?
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到这件事发生后仅仅一小时内相关讨论的转变，那么如果他公开作证数小时，会产生什么样的影响呢？

sentences.en: Because what you've had in the aftermath of his press statement, it's I think it's a fair inference from what we heard in that press conference that Bob Mueller was essentially
sentences.zh: 因为在他发表媒体声明之后，我认为从我们在那场新闻发布会上听到的内容可以得出一个公平的推论，即鲍勃·穆勒本质上是

sentences.en: referring impeachment to the United States Congress.
sentences.zh: 将弹劾问题移交给了美国国会。

sentences.en: We did not elect an authoritarian in chief.
sentences.zh: 我们选出的不是一位独裁者。

sentences.en: He should be subject to the checks and balances of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 他应该受到宪法制衡的约束。

sentences.en: And in this case, he's not doing that.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，他并没有这样做。

sentences.en: And I have said that I support opening an impeachment inquiry.
sentences.zh: 我已经说过，我支持开启弹劾调查。

sentences.en: I believe that the president obstructed justice and I would vote to impeach.
sentences.zh: 我相信总统妨碍了司法公正，我会投票支持弹劾。

sentences.en: Which is several prominent Democrats, including many that are running for president, come out
sentences.zh: 这使得几位著名的民主党人，包括许多正在竞选总统的人，站出来

sentences.en: and say it's time for impeachment using what Mueller said to say we should move forward with impeachment proceedings.
sentences.zh: 说现在是弹劾的时候了，利用穆勒所说的话来表示我们应该推进弹劾程序。

sentences.en: So you're saying if Mueller can move the public discourse that much with a prewritten statement
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，如果穆勒能用一份预先写好的声明如此大地推动公众舆论，

sentences.en: that he delivers that was essentially just like a glorified book report of his report.
sentences.zh: 那份声明本质上就像是他报告的一份美化版的读书报告。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Then how much could he move the public discourse if he sits for authentic back and forth conversation with members of a congressional committee?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果他坐下来与国会委员会成员进行真实的来回对话，他能多大程度上推动公众舆论呢？

sentences.en: Yes, because clearly some of Mueller's motivation today is to try and take his testimony off the table.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为很明显，穆勒今天的部分动机是试图将他的作证排除在议程之外。

sentences.en: But what he may have done is showed the power that his testimony could have.
sentences.zh: 但他可能已经展示了他的作证所能产生的力量。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: If he would be willing to give it.
sentences.zh: 如果他愿意作证的话。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's never cleared the president.
sentences.zh: 他从未宣布总统无罪。

sentences.en: And to hear the person who has investigated the president for the past two years say that is a pretty big deal.
sentences.zh: 听到过去两年调查总统的人这样说，这可是件大事。

sentences.en: I guess the question is, is it too late?
sentences.zh: 我想问题在于，现在是否太晚了？

sentences.en: Well, it's five weeks after the report came out.
sentences.zh: 嗯，距离报告发布已经过去五周了。

sentences.en: A lot has been cemented since then.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，很多事情已经定型了。

sentences.en: And if he had spoken earlier, would it have moved the narrative in a different direction?
sentences.zh: 如果他早点发言，叙事方向会改变吗？

sentences.en: We're hearing from Mueller, but we're hearing from him in what looks like the bottom of the ninth inning.
sentences.zh: 我们听到了穆勒的声音，但我们是在比赛进入第九局下半时才听到他的声音。

sentences.en: I don't know why we're hearing from him, but we now need to see whether it's actually going to do anything.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我们为什么会听到他的声音，但我们现在需要看看这是否真的会有所作为。

sentences.en: So did Mueller, here at the last gasp, sort of push things over the top in the house?
sentences.zh: 那么，穆勒在最后关头，是否在众议院推动了局势的发展？

sentences.en: That's sort of where we are right now.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们目前所处的境地。

sentences.en: And I guess we'll never really know what would have happened if he'd spoken earlier.
sentences.zh: 我想我们永远不会真正知道如果他早点发言会发生什么。

sentences.en: No, his style was to allow his word, his written word, to speak for itself.
sentences.zh: 不，他的风格是让他的文字，他的书面文字，不言自明。

sentences.en: That may not have gotten this to where he wanted it.
sentences.zh: 这可能并没有让他达到他想要的目的。

sentences.en: Does that mean that this is basically over?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着这一切基本上结束了？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: What I do know is that it did not move the House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, who has tried to stop her caucus from moving forward with impeachment.
sentences.zh: 我所知道的是，这并没有打动众议院议长南希·佩洛西，她一直试图阻止她的党团推进弹劾。

sentences.en: After Mueller's statement, she put out one of her own and she did not say this is time for impeachment.
sentences.zh: 在穆勒发表声明后，她也发表了自己的声明，但她并没有说现在是弹劾的时候。

sentences.en: So it certainly didn't move her.
sentences.zh: 所以这当然没有打动她。

sentences.en: And she's one of the most important people in whether this goes forward.
sentences.zh: 而她是决定此事是否推进的最重要人物之一。

sentences.en: Mike, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 迈克，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Wednesday night, seven weeks after Israelis voted in nationwide elections, Israel's government
sentences.zh: 周三晚上，在以色列举行全国大选七周后，以色列政府

sentences.en: said that it would hold a new election because Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu failed to form a coalition government.
sentences.zh: 表示将举行新的选举，因为总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡未能组建联合政府。

sentences.en: It was a major embarrassment for Netanyahu, who was convinced he had the influence to put together a government.
sentences.zh: 这对内塔尼亚胡来说是一个巨大的尴尬，他曾确信自己有影响力组建政府。

sentences.en: But in the end, a power struggle broke out between secular and religious factions of his proposed coalition, blocking his path.
sentences.zh: 但最终，他提议的联盟中的世俗派和宗教派别之间爆发了权力斗争，阻碍了他的道路。

sentences.en: And
sentences.zh: 而且

sentences.en: During a talk in his home state of Kentucky, Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell said
sentences.zh: 在肯塔基州家乡的一次演讲中，参议院多数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔表示

sentences.en: that Republicans would confirm a Supreme Court justice if a vacancy opened up during next year's presidential campaign.
sentences.zh: 如果明年总统竞选期间出现空缺，共和党人将会确认最高法院大法官的人选。

sentences.en: That directly contradicted his rationale for not confirming a justice in the final year of the Obama presidency.
sentences.zh: 这直接反驳了他当年在奥巴马总统任期最后一年不确认大法官人选的理由。

sentences.en: McConnell had argued that it was improper to hold confirmation hearings for Judge Merrick
sentences.zh: 麦康奈尔曾辩称，在选举年，在新总统选出并就职之前，为梅里克·加兰法官举行确认听证会是不合适的。

sentences.en: Garland in an election year before a new president had been chosen and inaugurated.
sentences.zh: 加兰。

sentences.en: An unusual outbreak of tornadoes has struck communities from Texas to Ohio, killing at least seven people and destroying hundreds of buildings.
sentences.zh: 一场罕见的龙卷风爆发袭击了从德克萨斯州到俄亥俄州的社区，造成至少七人死亡，数百座建筑物被毁。

sentences.en: The National Weather Service has reported more than 400 tornadoes over the past two weeks, with nearly 45 around Dayton, Ohio, alone.
sentences.zh: 国家气象局报告称，过去两周发生了400多起龙卷风，仅在俄亥俄州代顿市附近就有近45起。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日秀》的内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《地铁》的最新一集中，我和莎拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在你获取播客的任何地方收听。
